clue.text: Reading online periodical backwards is a fun activity

indicators.note: together with the later word, it tells the solver to read the letters in the opposite direction
reading something backwards means starting from its last letter and working toward its first

parts.note: an e-mag is an electronic magazine published on the web

explanation.surface: Someone claims that browsing a web magazine from back to front is good fun.
explanation.walkthrough: EMAG read from right to left gives GAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A game is a pastime played for enjoyment, which is a fun activity.

clue.text: Adult woman's clothing in set

indicators.note: in means the kept letters are placed inside the next word

parts.note: a set is a group

indicators.note: clothing is what covers the outside, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: outer letters of woman

explanation.surface: An adult woman's outfit is part of a set.
explanation.walkthrough: Clothing wants to be a noun for garments; it means covering, so the outside letters of woman go inside GROUP between O and U.
explanation.definitionFit: A grown-up is someone who has reached full maturity, an adult.

clue.text: Crazy morning with mistress…

parts.note: mad means crazy
a.m. marks the morning hours

explanation.surface: A wild morning spent with a lover, continued into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots carry the sentence on to the following clue, which shares the same racy story.
explanation.definitionFit: A madam is a woman in charge of a household or a brothel, a mistress in that sense.

clue.text: Pen divorce revision in capital

indicators.note: a revision changes and reorders text, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A lawyer drafts revisions to a divorce agreement somewhere in a state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Providence is the capital of the US state of Rhode Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Providence is the state seat of government of Rhode Island, so it is a capital city.

clue.text: …rated R, perhaps — and R is what, in Spanish?

parts.note: taken as written
qué is Spanish for what

explanation.surface: A film rated R, continuing the steamy story, and a query about the letter in Spanish.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the US film rating restricting under-17s, so perhaps marks an example rather than a definition word for word.
explanation.definitionFit: Risqué means slightly indecent or racy, the kind of content that earns a restricted rating.

clue.text: Aristocrat's price markdown, initially reduced by 99%

indicators.note: the first letter, taken as a roman numeral, is cut to a hundredth of its value, so it is swapped

parts.note: a discount is a reduction in price

explanation.surface: A nobleman's discount on prices, slashed by nearly all of it.
explanation.walkthrough: D is the roman numeral 500; cut by 99% it becomes 5, the numeral V. The definition is possessive (aristocrat is): read the 's as is.
explanation.definitionFit: A viscount is a British nobleman ranking above a baron and below an earl.

clue.text: Blue feathers found at landfills

parts.note: down is the soft fine plumage of birds
found at a place means located in it
landfills are rubbish dumps, the dumps

explanation.surface: Bird plumage turns up at garbage sites.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, soft feathers (down) found at landfills (the dumps) are down in the dumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Down in the dumps is an idiom meaning depressed or gloomy, which is what feeling blue means.

clue.text: Prehistoric chili (note: it's gone bad)

indicators.note: something gone bad has spoiled and changed form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A warning label on ancient stew: this chili has spoiled.
explanation.definitionFit: The Neolithic is the New Stone Age, a period long before written history.

clue.text: Naval officers:

parts.note: the definition: junior commissioned ranks at sea
the colon announces wordplay that our copy of the clue has lost

explanation.walkthrough: Our copy of this clue stops at the colon; whatever wordplay followed is missing from the source, so only the definition can be shown. The crossing letters confirm the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is the lowest commissioned rank in the US Navy, so ensigns are junior naval officers.

clue.text: Home for many people with a role to exploit: suppressing flavor in cigarettes, largely

indicators.note: largely means mostly, not all, so the end is dropped
to suppress is to hold down and keep in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: taken as written
an actor's part is a role
menthol is a minty flavoring added to cigarettes, cut short
to use someone is to exploit them

explanation.surface: A building full of people where someone plans to exploit a role while hiding menthol cigarettes.
explanation.walkthrough: Menthol is the minty flavor of some cigarettes; largely drops its final letter. The colon is only punctuation between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An apartment house is a residential building split into many flats, a home for many people.

clue.text: Die tragically, interrupting work for a king

indicators.note: something that ends tragically has gone badly wrong, so the letters are thrown out of order
to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: an opus is a piece of creative work
the three letters of this word, rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor dies dramatically partway through a work about a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits nicely: Oedipus is the tragic king of Sophocles's play, so the die-tragically scene belongs to him.
explanation.definitionFit: Oedipus is the legendary ruler of Thebes in Greek myth, a monarch made famous by Sophocles.

clue.text: Spotted records for sleep

parts.note: spotted means saw, past tense of see
logs are written records, like a ship's log

explanation.surface: Someone found blotchy records that are meant to track sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: To saw logs is American slang for snoring, so for sleeping soundly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawing logs is an informal idiom for being sound asleep, from the rasping noise of snoring.

clue.text: Foremost on our menu: crackers

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, and crazy letters do not stay in their given order

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A restaurant proudly puts crackers at the top of its menu.
explanation.walkthrough: Crackers looks like a food on the menu, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Numero uno is borrowed from Italian for number one, meaning the top or leading one.

clue.text: Fingering front of indentation (minor surface damage)

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: first letter of indentation
a ding is a small dent, say in a car door

explanation.surface: Fingering the start of a dent, someone checks some small surface damage.
explanation.walkthrough: To ID a suspect is to identify them; IDING is that verb's -ing form, written ID-ING.
explanation.definitionFit: To finger someone is slang for identifying them to police, which is ID-ing them.

clue.text: Hymns might be an afterthought, something offered to the poor

parts.note: a PS, a postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter
alms are gifts of money or food given to the poor

explanation.surface: A church scene: hymns sung as an afterthought to charity for the poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Psalms are sacred songs from the Bible, sung in worship like hymns.

clue.text: Where you might find medical professionals with unusual lab acumen

definitions.text: Where you might find medical professionals

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters are put in an irregular order

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Doctors and nurses in a lab show exceptional expertise.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramedics ride in an ambulance, the emergency vehicle carrying medical staff to patients.

clue.text: Superficially, skin irritations for singers?

indicators.note: superficially means only on the surface, so only the outside letters are kept

parts.note: outer letters of skin
itches are irritations of the skin

explanation.surface: It looks like a question about rashes that bother vocalists.
explanation.walkthrough: Singers has nothing to do with music: to sing is slang for informing on accomplices, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Snitches are informers, and an informer who talks to police is said in slang to sing.

clue.text: Most cheerful stories cause a shock on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside means wrapped around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to jolt is to give a shock
stories can be fibs or lies

explanation.surface: The happiest tales are the ones that cause a surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: Stories here means fibs, not tales of adventure.
explanation.definitionFit: Jolliest means merriest or happiest, the superlative of jolly.

clue.text: Revolutionary icon: baby or child on a ship

indicators.note: a revolution overturns the order of things, so these letters are reshuffled

parts.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: It reads like a caption about a famous rebel pictured as an infant or a young sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolutionary icon looks like Che Guevara and a definition, but revolutionary is the signal and icon plus baby is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabin boy is a young lad who serves officers and passengers aboard a vessel.

clue.text: Treacherous clue about writing implement in a workspace

indicators.note: treacherous means untrustworthy, so the letters cannot be trusted to stay in order
about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: the four letters of clue, rearranged
a Bic is a familiar brand of ballpoint pen

explanation.surface: A tricky crossword clue about a pen in an office.
explanation.walkthrough: Bic is a brand name used as a generic word for a ballpoint pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A cubicle is a small partitioned work area in an open-plan office.

clue.text: Left-leaning Catholic nephew embraces writer

indicators.note: leaning to the left means heading leftward, so the letters are read from right to left
to embrace is to hold within, so the answer lies inside the run of words

parts.note: letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A liberal Catholic family's nephew hugs a novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: Left-leaning sounds political; here it means read leftward.
explanation.definitionFit: A pencil is an instrument for writing, so it can be called a writer.

clue.text: Shady dealer hides last bit of money in sweater, vest and coat

indicators.note: shady means dubious and crooked, so these letters are twisted out of order
to hide something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: the six letters of dealer, rearranged

indicators.note: the last bit of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: last letter of money

explanation.surface: A crooked dealer stashes cash inside his warm clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Shady dealer looks like a crook; shady is the signal to rearrange dealer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wearing a sweater, vest and coat at once has put on several layers, so is layered.

clue.text: In return, made good item for infants

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the letters are read backward

parts.note: to make good a debt is to repay it

explanation.surface: Someone repaid a debt with something for babies.
explanation.walkthrough: A diaper is the American word for a nappy.
explanation.definitionFit: A diaper is the absorbent garment babies wear, so a basic item for infants.

clue.text: Eruption if Thunder's center were left among backup players

indicators.text: if Thunder's center were left among
indicators.note: the conditional tells the solver to swap one letter for another, with left supplying the newcomer

parts.note: the bench is where a team's reserves sit

indicators.note: 'center' keeps only the middle letter of 'Thunder'

parts.note: middle letter of thunder
L is the usual abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: It reads like basketball: the Oklahoma City Thunder's center has gone to sit with the reserves.
explanation.walkthrough: The Thunder are an NBA team, so center looks like a player's position; here it means the middle letter of thunder. In BENCH, the N becomes L.
explanation.definitionFit: A belch is a sudden noisy burst of gas from the stomach, an eruption.

clue.text: Laid-back vacation's souvenir? Indeed

parts.note: a lei is a garland of flowers given to visitors in Hawaii
indeed and surely both mean certainly

explanation.surface: It looks like a question: is a souvenir from a relaxed holiday really this?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a lei as just one example of a holiday souvenir. Laid-back looks like it describes the holiday, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisurely means unhurried and relaxed, the same as laid-back.

clue.text: Someone at breakfast is more tidy when starting late

indicators.note: starting late means the word begins one step on, so its opening letter is missing

parts.note: neater means more tidy

explanation.surface: A late riser at the breakfast table is tidier than usual.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone eating at a breakfast table is a diner, so an eater is a fair example.

clue.text: Puzzle: if it is too short, it could lead to prison violence?

parts.note: the surface reading: a brainteaser that is too brief

parts.words: if it is too short, it could lead to prison violence?
parts.note: the setter's reading: split the answer in two, an inmate plus the thing whose shortness means a quick temper

explanation.surface: A puzzle so short that it supposedly drives inmates to riot.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as CON FUSE: a con is a convict, and a person with a short fuse is quick to lose their temper, so a convict's short fuse could start a fight in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: To confuse someone is to baffle or bewilder them, which is what puzzle means as a verb.

clue.text: Father's pitch for musical celebrity

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father, plus the 's
pitch is black sticky tar

explanation.surface: A dad's sales pitch to promote his child as a famous singer.
explanation.walkthrough: Pitch looks musical or like a sales pitch; here it is the black stuff used to seal roads.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop star is a famous performer of popular music, a celebrity of that field.

clue.text: Basic alert: "enemy in turmoil"

indicators.note: turmoil is chaos and upheaval, so the letters are churned into a new order

parts.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A rudimentary military warning that the enemy is in disarray.
explanation.definitionFit: Elementary means simple and fundamental, a synonym of basic.

clue.text: At first, get free space to put your letters

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter only of the next word

parts.note: first letter of get
to rid is to free, as in rid of pests

explanation.surface: Advice to grab some free room to post your mail first.
explanation.walkthrough: Letters sounds like mail, but the solver's letters go in a crossword's squares.
explanation.definitionFit: The grid is the pattern of squares in which a solver writes the answer letters.
